## EMST role: Wildlife biologist (state variant, senior level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.45, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R15-wildlife-biologist/state:2684`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — senior L3
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — senior L3 *(distinguishing)*
- Detect and record wildlife by direct observation, sign and standardized surveys — senior L3
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — senior L3
- Adjudicate automated species detections using field-formed identification expertise — senior L3
- Assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions — senior L3
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — senior L3
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — senior L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — senior L1
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — senior L2
- Assess and monitor biodiversity across species and habitats — senior L3
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — senior L3

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions — 4.9% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses — 4.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata — 4.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Conduct ground or aerial counts of target species along defined survey units to support abundance estimation — 4.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol — 4.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Evaluate a habitat suitability map against field observations of use and condition, documenting where and why the model fails — 4.3% *(critical)*
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits — 3.4% *(needed at entry)*
- Apply zoonotic disease and personal safety precautions when handling wildlife, including protective equipment and decontamination — 3.4% *(needed at entry)*
- Train seasonal crew members in survey protocol and identification cues, checking each trainee's detections against an experienced observer — 3.4%
- Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions — 3.4% *(needed at entry)*
- Integrate habitat findings into land-use or project plans as specific measures that avoid or reduce effects on species of concern — 3.4%
- Observe animal movement, foraging and breeding behaviour at study sites, recording behaviour and habitat context on standardized forms — 3.4% *(needed at entry)*

## EMST role: Fisheries and aquatic biologist (state variant, senior level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.5, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R16-fisheries-aquatic-biologist/state:2684`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Manage fish populations and habitats to stated conservation and harvest objectives — senior L3 *(distinguishing)*
- Conduct fisheries stock assessments and develop management advice — senior L3
- Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols — senior L2
- Operate small boats and work safely on water in aquatic, coastal and marine field settings — senior L2
- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — senior L3
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — senior L3
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — senior L1
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — senior L3
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — senior L1
- Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination — senior L2
- Operate fish hatchery and aquatic propagation programmes — senior L2
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — senior L3

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Sample fish populations by electrofishing, netting or hydroacoustics following the survey protocol to estimate abundance and size structure — 5.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Recommend harvest regulations, stocking or habitat actions for a fishery from population assessment results and angler objectives — 5.2% *(critical)*
- Assess water quality and habitat conditions limiting a fish population, identifying the factors management can change — 4.1%
- Estimate age, growth and mortality of a fish population from scale or otolith readings and catch-curve data — 4.1%
- Fit a stock assessment model to catch, survey and biological data, documenting model diagnostics and retrospective patterns — 4.1%
- Apply a data-limited assessment method to a stock with sparse catch and survey data, stating the uncertainty in reference points — 4.1%
- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Execute person-overboard, capsize and cold-water immersion procedures for a small-boat crew during drills and real events — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Work sampling gear such as grabs, nets, sondes or traps over the side of a small vessel, keeping crew clear of lines and winches — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Screen field measurement results against applicable water-quality criteria before leaving the site, triggering resampling or notification when an exceedance appears — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*

## EMST role: Restoration and land stewardship project lead (state variant, journey/senior level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.4, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R09-restoration-project-lead/state:2684`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Implement ecological restoration treatments and adapt them to site response — journey L2, senior L3 *(distinguishing)*
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — journey L2, senior L3
- Work alongside landowners, permittees, volunteers and communities on the land — journey L2, senior L3
- Read site history and reference conditions from landscape evidence — journey L2, senior L3
- Deliver environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality — journey L2, senior L3
- Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action — journey L2, senior L2
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — journey L2, senior L3
- Recognize and assess ecosystems that have crossed into novel states — journey L2, senior L3 *(distinguishing)*
- Administer contracts, grants and intergovernmental agreements — journey L2, senior L3
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1, senior L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1, senior L1
- Lead field crews and transfer field judgment to novices — journey L2, senior L3
- Plan and run field campaigns and remote logistics — journey L2, senior L3
- Manage client and partner scope for environmental work — journey L2, senior L2
- Develop proposals and grant applications for environmental work — journey L2, senior L2
- Apply systems thinking across ecological, institutional and technical systems — journey L2, senior L2
- Detect, treat and monitor invasive species in the field — journey L2, senior L2
- Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments — journey L2, senior L3
- Develop and manage partnerships for shared environmental goals — senior L2

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Adapt restoration techniques at a site when monitoring shows plantings, structures or soils are not responding as planned, recording the change — 7.7% *(critical)*
- Read site response after a restoration treatment, such as sediment capture, wetting, establishment or browse, recording evidence at fixed photo points — 7.6% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Build low-tech process-based structures such as beaver dam analogues or post-assisted log structures, placing each from field reading of flow and channel form — 3.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Develop a restoration plan that accounts for the species interdependencies the target community needs to persist. — 3.8%
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol — 3.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Integrate habitat findings into land-use or project plans as specific measures that avoid or reduce effects on species of concern — 3.8%
- Determine whether restoration to historical conditions is feasible at a site, documenting the thresholds, drivers and costs that limit recovery — 3.8% *(critical)*
- Interpret fire scars, stumps, soil horizons and legacy structures at a site to reconstruct its disturbance and land-use history — 3.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Reconcile field evidence of site history with maps, aerial photographs, management records and accounts from people who know the site — 3.8%
- Define the monitoring questions, indicators and decision triggers for a plan or programme so that each indicator answers a stated management question. — 3.8% *(critical)*
- Design the sampling frame, allocation and sample size for a monitoring programme, documenting the inference each design choice supports. — 3.8%
- Conduct a joint field visit with a landowner or permittee, walking the site together and recording both parties' observations — 3.8% *(needed at entry)*
